# jenkins_node (Resource)

Manages a permanent (static) agent node within Jenkins, launched as an inbound agent.

Changing `name` replaces the node. Every other attribute is updated in place through the
node's `config.xml`, and a connected agent stays connected. A connected agent picks up a
new `remote_fs` or `web_socket` only when it next connects. Settings the resource does not
manage, such as other node properties or the agent's work directory options, keep the values
they have on the controller. Connect the agent out-of-band with the secret Jenkins issues for
it, which the `jenkins_node_secret` data source reads.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "jenkins_node" "example" {
  name          = "linux-agent-01"
  num_executors = 2
  remote_fs     = "/home/jenkins/agent"
  labels        = "linux docker"
  description   = "Managed by Terraform"
}

# Only builds jobs whose label expression names team-a, so a job with no
# label never lands on it. A label reserves nothing by itself, since any job
# can name it: the job restriction refuses every job outside the team-a
# folder (needs the job-restrictions plugin). The agent connects over
# WebSocket, through the controller's HTTP(S) port.
resource "jenkins_node" "team_a" {
  name       = "team-a-agent-01"
  remote_fs  = "/home/jenkins/agent"
  labels     = "team-a"
  mode       = "EXCLUSIVE"
  web_socket = true

  job_restriction = {
    regex = "^team-a/.*"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the node. Changing this forces a new node to be created.
- `remote_fs` (String) The absolute path to the agent's root/working directory on the agent machine (e.g. `/home/jenkins/agent`). A connected agent keeps using the previous path until it reconnects.

### Optional

- `description` (String) A human readable description of the node.
- `job_restriction` (Attributes) Restricts the node to the jobs whose name matches a regular expression: the node refuses every other build, whatever labels it carries. Needs the Job Restrictions plugin (`job-restrictions`) on the controller. Removing the attribute removes the restriction. A restriction of another type set in the UI is not read, and is replaced when this attribute is set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--job_restriction))
- `labels` (String) A space-separated list of labels used to target the node from job configurations, with no leading or trailing whitespace.
- `mode` (String) How Jenkins schedules builds on the node: `NORMAL` (the default) uses the node as much as possible, including for jobs with no label; `EXCLUSIVE` only builds jobs whose label expression matches the node.
- `num_executors` (Number) The number of concurrent builds the node can run, at least `1`. Defaults to `1`.
- `web_socket` (Boolean) The *Use WebSocket* option of the inbound launcher: the agent connects over WebSocket through the controller's HTTP(S) port instead of the TCP agent port. Jenkins hands it to agents that read their launch arguments from the controller; an agent started with `-webSocket` connects over WebSocket whatever this is set to. A connected agent keeps its current transport until it reconnects. Defaults to `false`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The name of the node, which is also its unique identifier.

<a id="nestedatt--job_restriction"></a>
### Nested Schema for `job_restriction`

Required:

- `regex` (String) Java regular expression the full name of the job (folders included) must match. The plugin accepts every job when the expression does not compile.

Optional:

- `check_short_name` (Boolean) The plugin's *Check short name* option. Defaults to `false`. Job Restrictions `242.v6edda_c9e4ca_f` stores it but matches the full name either way.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Jenkins nodes can be imported by their name.
terraform import jenkins_node.example linux-agent-01
```
